blocks.x: Grid-edge visibility and orchestration — curtailment of renewables down 31% and congestion costs down 24% on a network built for one direction
Identity withheld — a DSO whose network was engineered for power flowing one way and whose rooftops had other plans. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline year measured the wrong-way traffic: 4.1 GWh of solar curtailed for lack of visibility below the secondary substation, congestion costs rising each quarter, and connection queues growing because the network's real capacity was unknown.
Low-voltage observability was nearly zero; flexibility offers existed but nothing could schedule them safely. The grid team planned with worst-case assumptions because best-case was invisible.

We built the grid-edge spine: LV-level monitoring where it mattered and model-based observability where it didn't, flexibility assets registered with their true envelope, an orchestration layer scheduling flexibility against congestion forecasts with the DSO's safety envelope enforced, and connection assessments running on measured headroom. The network found capacity it had been refusing.
